proof_summary: Legendre’s formula reduces the divisibility to floor inequalities at each prime-power level: the nonnegative Landau function \(L_m(n)=\lfloor8n/m\rfloor+\lfloor n/m\rfloor-\lfloor4n/m\rfloor-\lfloor3n/m\rfloor-\lfloor2n/m\rfloor\) is at least \(1\) whenever \(m\ge 8r\) and a multiple of \(m\) lies in \((kn,kn+r]\), as follows by analyzing \(n\bmod m\) for \(k=1,2,3\). Hence only levels \(p^j<8r\) incur a defect—at most \(r\) per level and over at most \(r+2\) levels—and \(C=((8r)!)^{r(r+3)}\) supplies enough valuation at every such small prime.
